title: Why Hampton fired Illinois Jacquet over Flying Home
summary: Cobb relays what Hampton and Gladys told him: Jacquet cursed Hampton on stage for cutting off Flying Home and was given notice.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But now, the thing you, Arnett, was Illinois leaving at this point or --
He was -- Hamp had given him his notice.
Gave his notice? Do you know why?
Well, do you want to say it or not? You don't have to.

Well, what happened is -- or what I heard. Now, I don't know (inaudible) and I got this from Hamp and Gladys, that Hamp had cut him off from playing Flying Home, and he turned around on stage and he cussed Hamp (inaudible) he get through when he get ready. So Hamp cut the band in on

him on the outchorus course and went to the B flat (inaudible). And that's where they had the confusion. And so from that point Gladys said, give him his notice. He had told Hamp I couldn't read when he finally said he was getting me in the band. He said I couldn't read. That's what Hamp said. Now, I don't know.

I stayed with it five years. I put it like that. Now, whatever I did, it must have been all right for five years. But I didn't get into that problems and nothing like that, but he called Hamp and cussed him out on the stage in front of the microphone and an audience, told him he'd get off when he get ready. You know Gladys is not going to permit that.
